Austria-Hungary lost the war, then the peace. The Treaty of Saint-Germain, signed on 10 September 1919, shows who got what.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Bohemia and Moravia, plus part of Austrian Silesia, became the core of Czechoslovakia. Galicia went to the re-established Polish Republic, and Bukovina to Romania.

2/ Italy received South Tyrol and Trentino, the Tarvisio area, the Austrian Littoral and Istria. The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes got Bosnia and Herzegovina, much of Dalmatia, Carniola and Lower Styria.
3/ Southern Carinthia was left to a plebiscite rather than settled at the table. Austria's army was capped at 30,000 volunteers and conscription was abolished.
4/ The republic had called itself German-Austria. The treaty forced it to drop 'German'. Article 88 also made union with Germany depend on the League of Nations Council agreeing to it.
5/ Austria lost over 60% of the prewar Austrian Empire's territory, per Wikipedia. Article 177 made it accept responsibility for the war. Reparations were never defined or collected.
6/ Hungary's terms came in a separate treaty, which is why the map leaves it as its own block. Saint-Germain itself came into force on 16 July 1920.
A state that lost most of its territory in one signature. Was the peace too harsh? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
